turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mrs Pillay, come on through. I'll do the blood pressure quick before the doctor. Left arm ok?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, please use the left. The right still feels a bit bruised from the drip at the op, they poked around three times, and my daughter kept saying the bruise looked like a map of the Cape, shame, all the way to the wrist.
[SEG0003] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Hold still please. One thirty eight over eighty four. Pulse seventy two. Oxygen ninety eight percent.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Is one thirty eight alright? The chemist last month said it was higher and my girl wrote it down, but the paper is in her car. She's on the parking meter outside, it only gives an hour, and she was cross about the robot by the entrance.
[SEG0005] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): We just need today's. Doctor's ready, you can go in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Mrs Pillay. Sit. What's brought you today?

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): The six week check after the hip replacement, doctor. The right one. They told me at the hospital I must come and show you the wound and how I'm walking. My daughter wanted to sit in but the parking is hopeless, so I came through on my own.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hip sore?

[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, ja, an ache for the whole six weeks, not the terrible pain of the first two weeks. Now I'd call it a four out of ten. It comes when I get up from the chair or I walk to the gate, and at night if I lie on the right side. The Panado takes the edge off in about an hour.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stiff?

[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, mornings, ja, the right hip, about half an hour till I've got to the kitchen. Then it eases. The physio said move it, so I do the little exercises on the bed, because my neighbour's hip locked and she went back to theatre.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Stick?

[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja. Left hand, opposite the sore hip, like they showed me. Indoors, in the passage, I sometimes leave it, but outside the pavement by the flats is all broken so the stick comes with me. I'm not brave enough without it yet.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Wound leaking? Red? Hot?

[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that. It's closed and dry, a thin line, and the clips came out at two weeks. My daughter checks with a torch every night, no ooze and no smell, she's very strict about it.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll look. Wound's healed. Walking with the stick is fine. Any swelling in the right calf?

[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No swelling. I measure it against the other leg every evening because of the clot talk before the op. Same size, not hot, and the calf doesn't hurt, the ache stays in the hip.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Calf's soft. No swelling.
[SEG0019] person_3 (DOCTOR): Tablets?

[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): The asprin, Ecotrin, for the clots, they want three months of it after the hip. And Panado when the hip nags. I stopped the zolpidem, the sleeping tablet from the hospital, after the first week. It made me foggy and I was scared I'd fall on the way to the loo.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ecotrin, what dose?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, one tablet, eighty one milligrams, every morning. I swallow it after porridge so my stomach doesn't burn. I haven't missed a day. My daughter puts it by the kettle.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): Panado dose?

[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Two of the five hundred milligram tablets, so that's a thousand milligrams, by mouth, up to three times a day, only if it's sore. Some quiet days I just do morning and bedtime. They said not to go over that and not to mix in other pain tablets.
[SEG0025] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drug reactions? Any allergy?

[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, penicilin, a proper one. Around when I was fifty the dentist gave me a penicilin injection for an abscess, and within an hour I had a rash everywhere and my lips swelled right up. Emergency gave me an injection to settle it, and I haven't taken it since. I tell the chemist every single time.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): Rash and swollen lips. No penicillin for you. Anything else?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, no, just the penicilin. Panado I've used for years, Ecotrin too, no trouble. I'm fine with food.
[SEG0029] person_3 (DOCTOR): Hip's healing as it should. No sign of a clot.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh that's a relief, doctor, I was lying awake thinking about those clots. My cousin had one after a flight, not the same thing I know, but you do think.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep swallowing the Ecotrin every morning until the three months is up. Panado only when the hip is sore, same dose, not extra.

[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, I'll finish the box. My daughter counts them on a Sunday. Three months from the op means I've got about another six weeks of the asprin, if I've counted the weeks right. I think the op was six weeks ago Tuesday.
[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): Walk every day. Stick stays for outside until you feel steady. If the calf swells or the wound opens, come in the same day. Don't sit on it.

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): And church? It's only down the road but there are steps, and the aunties will want to hug me and I'm scared they'll pull me off balance. I haven't been since the op and I miss it.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): Steps are fine if you take them one at a time with the stick. No driving until you can do an emergency stop.

[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I haven't driven. My daughter does it, well actually it's a little Polo not a bakkie, she fetches the groceries. I won't touch the car till you say. I'd be terrified in the traffic by the mall.
[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): Good. Back here in three months.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Three months, not sooner? If I'm doing well I mean. The physio is still twice a week at the rooms by the shops, should I keep that going the whole time?
[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): Keep the physio. Three months with me unless something changes.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): And the scar, can I put tissue oil on it now that it's closed? My daughter bought a bottle, the pink one, I haven't opened it because I didn't want to mess the wound.
[SEG0041] person_3 (DOCTOR): Dry and closed, yes, plain moisturiser is fine. Don't soak it in the bath yet.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Only showers, I know, I use the plastic chair in the shower so I don't slip. My daughter put the non-slip mat down the first week, it was a whole production.
[SEG0043] person_3 (DOCTOR): That's it. Reception will book you.
[SEG0044] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Mrs Pillay, three months, morning clinic. I'll give you a card. Your daughter's still outside?

[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Ja, she'll be stressing about the meter. Tell her it's three months, she'll write it in her book, she writes everything. Thank you, hey, I feel better knowing the calf is alright.
[SEG0046] person_1 (CLINICAL_STAFF): Card's here. Take care on the steps.

spec.situation: Older patient six weeks after a hip replacement with a daughter; wound healed; walks with a stick; takes aspirin for clots and painkiller; swelling of the calf asked about and denied.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

omissions.text: Right calf pain/tenderness was specifically denied by the patient ('the calf doesn't hurt'); only absence of swelling was recorded.
Patient reported the right calf was not hot/warm ('same size, not hot'), an asked-and-answered negative finding relevant to DVT/infection that was not recorded.
Doctor examined the right calf as soft ('Calf's soft'), an examination finding not recorded.

Ecotrin/aspirin was to be taken for a total of 3 months after surgery, and at this visit the patient had about 6 weeks remaining; the recorded plan omits the remaining duration context stated in the consultation.
Zolpidem was stopped because it caused fogginess and the patient feared falling when going to the toilet at night; only discontinuation was recorded, not the adverse effect/reason.
Penicillin allergy history included onset within an hour after a penicillin injection for a dental abscess and treatment in emergency with an injection; only the reaction was recorded.
Patient denied any other drug allergies/reactions besides penicillin ('no, just the penicillin').
